set.body:
Objective:
Freeze Frame as a general relational library incubating under ScalaFIM naming but architecturally independent of ScalaFIM domain modules and Gale. Prove the defining Scala 3.7+ API before committing to storage or engine internals, and record how a later extraction and rename would work.

Architecture decisions:
- Incubation uses ScalaFIM package and artifact conventions; neutral or frame4s naming is deferred until an actual extraction.
- No Frame core API imports ScalaFIM domain or Gale types. Package ownership and dependency ownership are separate questions.
- Frame[Schema] is an immutable resolved logical plan; DynamicFrame is the runtime-schema frontend; Expr[A] is a typed expression; Table[Schema] is materialized columnar data.
- Runtime schemas are facts; named-tuple schema types are evidence obtained at one checked promotion boundary.
- Dynamic and typed APIs lower to one resolved logical IR, and typed erasure preserves that exact plan and runtime schema.
- Plans contain immutable source descriptions, not open resources, backend values, or captured closures.
- Pure logical normalization is distinct from backend physical optimization.
- The local interpreter is the semantic oracle; production engines, formats, Gale, and ScalaFIM ntab are adapters or consumers.

Typelevel-candidate posture:
- Keep the pure logical core dependency-light; Cats Effect and FS2 belong at the resource-safe execution boundary where they solve a named problem.
- Select an OSI-approved license and record contribution provenance before reusable Frame code accumulates.
- Treat Typelevel affiliation as a later application based on a working independent library, not as permission to use org.typelevel names now.

Acceptance:
- A written architecture contract records current ScalaFIM naming, dependency direction, package/module layout, core/non-core boundaries, error ADTs, resource ownership, and the controlled rename/extraction procedure.
- A Scala 3.7+ compile spike demonstrates DynamicFrame binding, promotion to Frame[Schema], named-tuple expression scopes, typed projection and withColumn, grouping, inner join, outer-side nullability, and compile-time rejection of missing or mistyped fields.
- The spike distinguishes Expr[A] from nullable Expr[Option[A]] or equivalent evidence, with nullability separate from logical type and physical encoding.
- API sketches prove a pure plan, FS2 Stream[F, RecordBatch], Resource[F, Table] collection for resource-backed data, and pure logical explain without opening a source.
- Structured dynamic binding and planning failures use explicit ADTs.
- Compile-time behavior is measured on representative narrow and wide schemas.
- The spike runs on JVM and Scala.js or records a concrete compiler/platform blocker without weakening the design.
